intro.title: How Eleva works, piece by piece.
intro.lead: This page walks through the whole system, module by module, with the real product screens. It starts at the org chart and the role catalog, goes through the rubric the AI assembles from a curated question bank, and ends at the Chilean regulation everything is aligned to.

system.lead: Org chart, role catalog, question bank, rubrics per role, weighted perspectives, stages and results: each piece feeds the next.

estructura.runningHead: Org chart · Role catalog · AI match
estructura.title: Every role in the school, modeled properly.
estructura.lead: Not only teachers: leadership, education assistants, special-needs (PIE) staff, administrative staff, the board and the school owner. A role catalog with complete coverage, each role with a name, aliases, gender variants and reporting and evaluation relationships.

blocks.label: Org chart
blocks.title: The school's org chart, by year.
blocks.body: A tree of roles per year, with a Current view and a Proposed view from the catalog. Each node shows the person holding the role. The tree flags orphan roles (1 orphan in the example). "Review hierarchy" checks the structure and "Improve tree with AI" proposes how to order it. You decide what to apply.

rows.value: Review hierarchy · Improve tree with AI

blocks.label: Role catalog
blocks.title: Complete coverage, with the right names.
blocks.body: Each catalog role has a code, a family, aliases, names in Chilean Spanish and English, and gender variants. It declares who it reports to and whom it evaluates. It includes education assistants: classroom assistant, school-bus assistant, general services, receptionist, risk-prevention officer. It exports and imports as JSON and is applied to a school.

pauta.title: From the curated bank to a complete rubric for every role.
pauta.lead: The bank is curated: questions written by psychologists and evaluation experts, aligned to Chilean regulation. Each one declares its area, its dimension, which 360° perspectives can answer it, its priority, its weight and the law behind it. The AI selects by dimension, perspective, priority and regulation and assembles the role's complete rubric; you review it before using it.

proceso.title: A real 360°, with a six-stage flow.
proceso.lead: The school defines the weightings. Stages are configured centrally for every school of a school owner, and each school can adjust them.

weights.label: How much does each perspective weigh?
weights.sub: They define the final calculation. They must add up to exactly 100.

perspectives.desc: Each person evaluates their own performance

stages.label: Process stages

items.name: In Feedback
items.desc: The evaluator sends the evaluation to the evaluee for feedback

items.name: Finalized
items.desc: Evaluation finalized; its results count in reports

items.name: Closed
items.desc: Definitive closure; only an administrator can reopen it

stages.central: Central configuration: defines which stages of the flow are available by default for all schools, by perspective type. Each school can override this configuration on its own stages page.
stages.freeze: Changes apply to new processes: each process freezes its flow when generated, so historical processes keep the configuration they were created with.

plate.caption: Default stages per perspective · Central configuration · Manager-Subordinate
plate.alt: Central stage configuration: six stages from 0 to 5, three marked Always active and a toggle on the others.

resultados.title: Achievement per domain, and what to improve.
resultados.lead: Each evaluation is answered on a 1-to-5 Likert scale. Achievement is calculated per domain according to its weighting, and each domain receives an improvement suggestion. Finalized evaluations count in reports.

sugerencia.label: Improvement suggestion · per domain
sugerencia.text: After answering, each domain receives an improvement suggestion written from the answers. It is a starting point for feedback, not a verdict.

ia.title: The AI proposes. The school decides.
ia.lead: The AI steps in at three concrete points of the system. In all three, the last word is yours.

rows.name: Role match
rows.proposes: For each unassigned role in your org chart, it recommends catalog templates with a confidence percentage and explains its reasoning: "Name and description identical to ASIST_AULA_BAS. Child of the Primary Homeroom Teacher, consistent as direct classroom support for that cycle." If the tree does not fit, it proposes how to improve it.
rows.decides: You pick an option with "Choose", or describe what is missing or what you are looking for and receive a new proposal.

rows.name: Generated rubric
rows.proposes: It assembles a role's evaluation rubric from the curated question bank, selecting by dimension, perspective, priority and regulation. The result is the role's complete rubric, with its dimensions and the regulations and frameworks it evaluates.
rows.decides: You review the rubric, grouped by framework and area, before using it in a process.

rows.name: Improvement suggestion
rows.proposes: After answering, it proposes one improvement suggestion per domain.
rows.decides: Feedback stays between people: the suggestion is a starting point, not a result.

ia.quoteStart: The AI will propose the best solution;
ia.never: The AI does not evaluate, does not decide results and does not write regulation.

normativa.runningHead: Every question, traced to the law
normativa.title: Every question, traced to Chilean regulation.
normativa.lead: Each role's rubric lists the national regulation and professional frameworks it aligns with; the Director rubric and the Asistente de Aula Básica rubric do not cite the same laws. Each question carries its laws as tags: Ley Karin, Carrera Docente, MBDLE, Personal Data Protection 2024, School Coexistence. The result is consistent, defensible evaluations.
